clinician.trajectory_summary: A 75-year-old woman with chronic renal insufficiency presented to the emergency department with vomiting, diarrhea, confusion, epigastric pain, and weight loss. She had recently experienced acute renal failure due to severe dehydration from diarrhea. Physical examination revealed a circumferential rectal lesion on digital rectal examination. Colonoscopy identified a giant polyp of the rectum occupying three-quarters of the luminal circumference with 8-9 cm cranial-caudal extension. Biopsy confirmed a villous adenoma with focal high-grade dysplasia. Laboratory analysis at admission revealed severe electrolyte depletion (hyponatremia 124 mmol/L, hypokalemia 3.1 mmol/L) and acute renal failure (creatinine 318.24 μmol/L, hyperazotemia 188 mg/dL). Surgical resection was performed, resulting in complete normalization of electrolytes, full recovery of renal function, and resolution of gastrointestinal symptoms. At 10-month follow-up, the patient remained in good condition with no recurrence and normal renal function.
